blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Managing order fulfilment in practice means turning a promise into a parcel, reliably, for thousands of orders a day. The promise is made the moment the customer clicks 'buy'. From that second, a silent chain of small actions must happen in order — and no step can be skipped or delayed without the customer eventually noticing.

Good fulfilment managers track three things obsessively: order cycle time (how long from click to door?), first-time accuracy (what percentage go out right the first time?), and exception rate (how many orders need special handling?). These three numbers, reviewed daily, catch almost every problem before it becomes a customer complaint.

The quiet lesson of fulfilment is that customers forgive the occasional mistake, but they never forgive a chain of them — or the feeling that nobody is watching.

items.q: According to the text, when is the promise to the customer made?
options: When the manager reviews the numbers
items.why: "The promise is made the moment the customer clicks 'buy'."

items.q: Which three metrics do good fulfilment managers track?
options: Fill rate, discounts, and delivery cost
Order cycle time, first-time accuracy, and exception rate
items.why: "order cycle time… first-time accuracy… and exception rate."

items.q: According to the text, what do the three numbers achieve when reviewed daily?
options: They replace the need for a warehouse team
They reduce the cost of shipping
They guarantee no mistake ever happens
They catch almost every problem before it becomes a complaint
items.why: "reviewed daily, catch almost every problem before it becomes a customer complaint."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A single delayed step can eventually be noticed by the customer
One isolated mistake is usually forgiven
Customers dislike feeling that nobody is watching
Reviewing the metrics once a quarter is enough to stay in control
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste que os números são revistos DIARIAMENTE; revisar por trimestre contraria a tese.

items.q: What does "the feeling that nobody is watching" suggest about customers?
options: They only care about the price of the parcel
They expect a perfect record with zero errors
They lose trust when errors seem unmonitored, not just when errors occur
items.why: Inferência: o cliente perdoa o erro isolado, mas não a sensação de descontrole — a percepção de que ninguém acompanha.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily treinando o novo gestor de fulfilment. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, welcome aboard. Every morning at eight thirty, before I answer a single email, I open one screen. Three numbers. That's it.

The first is fill rate — the share of orders we can ship complete from stock. If it drops below ninety-five per cent, I don't wait for a report; I walk down to the warehouse and ask why. Below ninety-five, we're quietly losing revenue, order by order.

The second is on-time delivery. This is the one the customer actually feels. You can get everything else right, but if the parcel lands late, that's the number that shows up in the complaints.

The third is order accuracy — did we send the right item, to the right person, first time? Get this wrong and you pay three times: the return, the reship, and the damaged relationship.

Here's what I want you to remember. Orders are received, checked, and dispatched the same way every single day. This job isn't about heroics on a bad afternoon; it's about consistency. If you know your three numbers before nine, you're in control. If you don't, the day is already running you.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Emily do every morning at 8:30 before answering emails?
options: She reviews the previous day's complaints
She walks through the whole warehouse
She opens one screen with three numbers
items.why: "Every morning at eight thirty… I open one screen. Three numbers."

items.q: According to Emily, what happens when fill rate drops below 95%?
options: The company is quietly losing revenue
items.why: "Below ninety-five, we're quietly losing revenue, order by order."

items.q: Which metric does Emily say the customer 'actually feels'?
items.why: "The second is on-time delivery. This is the one the customer actually feels."

items.q: When Emily says you 'pay three times' for a wrong order, what does she imply?
options: Three managers must approve the fix
The item costs three times more to reship
A single accuracy error is far more costly than it first appears
The customer is charged three times
items.why: Inferência: o retorno, o reenvio e o dano ao relacionamento mostram que o erro custa muito mais que o item.

items.q: What is Emily's main message about the fulfilment manager's job?
options: It is mostly about hiring more warehouse staff
It rewards dramatic effort on difficult days
It depends on answering emails as fast as possible
It is about consistency and knowing your numbers, not heroics
items.why: Inferência: "This job isn't about heroics… It's about consistency" — controlar os três números diariamente.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We track our error rate obsessively, checking it several times a day." Obsessively means…
items.why: Obsessively = obsessivamente: com atenção constante e intensa.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Our ___ measures how long it takes from the click to the parcel reaching the door."
items.why: Order cycle time = tempo de ciclo do pedido: do clique até a entrega.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Only three per cent of orders need special handling, so our ___ is very low."
items.why: Exception rate = taxa de exceções: pedidos que exigem tratamento especial.

items.q: "When a parcel arrives late, we usually receive a complaint within hours." A complaint is…
items.why: Complaint = reclamação: uma manifestação de insatisfação.

items.q: First-time accuracy is best described as…
options: the share of orders sent out correctly on the first attempt
how fast the first order of the day ships
the number of new customers each day
items.why: First-time accuracy = acerto na primeira vez: pedidos enviados corretamente já na primeira tentativa.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem na gestão de operações e fulfilment. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The operations director still has to sign off on the new dispatch process." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new tracking system to one warehouse at a time." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "The team agreed to fix the exceptions but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, não foi feito.

items.q: "Trimming five minutes off packing won't move the needle on our cycle time." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "When accuracy slips, small errors quickly add up." To add up means to…
items.why: Add up = acumular-se; erros pequenos somam e viram um problema grande.
